Cyber Attack Disrupts Ukraine’s Payment Networks and Logistics

A major cyber attack is disrupting Ukraine’s national payments infrastructure, with widespread knock-on effects on logistics, retail, and trade across the country. The incident, which began late Tuesday evening, has crippled payment processing networks and hindered electronic transactions at ports, railway terminals, and in physical retail outlets nationwide.

According to the State Cybersecurity Coordination Centre, “unknown actors initiated a coordinated attack targeting central payment routing nodes and transaction authentication modules.” The attack has rendered thousands of payment terminals inoperative and forced several logistics hubs—including the key Black Sea port of Novomorsk—to temporarily halt cargo clearance.

The National Retailers’ Association of Ukraine reported that “card payments are failing in over 70 percent of outlets,” and supermarkets in Kyiv, Lviv, Dnipro and Odesa have reverted to cash-only operations. Queue lengths have surged as businesses scramble to update point-of-sale systems and verify payments manually.

Rail and trucking operators are also experiencing delays. Anton Bilash, spokesperson for the National Road Freight Union, stated, “Our members report that payment verification failures are blocking access to several major depots. Shipments are being delayed by hours or cancelled outright.”

The Ukrainian Digital Security Agency has advised businesses to “activate emergency payment protocols and verify all digital communications,” warning that the full extent of the attack remains unclear. “We are working with international partners to identify the source and restore normal operations,” said acting director Olena Kovalenko.

Industry analysts estimate that the disruption could cost the Ukrainian economy up to $120 million per day, depending on the duration of the attack. “The interconnected nature of payments and logistics amplifies the impact,” said Vadym Hryn, senior analyst at Eastern Markets Consultancy.

At the time of writing, the situation remains unresolved, with cyber teams racing to restore critical systems and businesses bracing for further disruption.
